heading: The Valley's home inventory is rising, but affordability remains out of reach

paragraphs.text: Over the past decade, the median sale price of a home increased 75% in the McAllen metro and 104% in the Brownsville-Harlingen metro.
By comparison, median household income increased 63% in the McAllen metro and 67% in the Brownsville metro over the same period, meaning wages have not kept pace with the cost of buying a home.

“Now, a year later, we’re starting to see people say, ‘Oh my goodness, I cannot pay these taxes. It’s way too much for me. Not on the salary I’m making, so I need to get rid of this property,’” she said.
